scope: Actual ordinary QMI data proxy SIGKILL, retained original-owner fence, and controlled original-SIM generation-change recovery with explicit subsequent data enable; not automatic proxy-loss recovery
harnessFindings: Private helper imports and continuation indentation were repaired before any injected signal; existing manager/port acquisition was not replayed.

The original ModemManager-owned proxy did not exit during a bounded absence wait despite zero established clients. The owning temporary manager was stopped normally, process/socket absence confirmed, then the private proxy was cold-started before the manager and original port inhibitors were re-established. No serving proxy was adopted or individually killed to prepare the case.
limits: Proxy-loss automatic data recovery did not pass: a fresh proxy served, but the old transport and durable fence remained unresolved. Controlled maintenance and an explicit new data enable were required.
The original independent owner survived. This does not prove cleanup after death of that owner, machine/power loss or recovery by force-deleting a journal.
Main/owner automatic restarts were disabled in this private fixture to retain the original capability. Shipping Compose defaults and systemd dependency cascades were not fault-tested here.
The first actual public query used IPv6; the post-maintenance query used IPv4 under dual-stack configuration. Post-maintenance end-to-end IPv6 was not independently proved by that query.
This is ordinary module data, not Host IMS voice/session recovery. Other active-call/daemon/host failures, browser audio, remote IVR, hardware/provisioning/provider combinations remain open.
Implementation was unchanged; prior software suites are referenced only, with no new Go/frontend/race/build execution.
